rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects a definition that presupposes intuitive knowledge of belief: if belief’s essence is self-evident, the same could be said of knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن هذا التعريف لا يتم إلا إذا ادعينا أن علمنا بماهية الإعتقاد علم بديهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining knowledge as absence of its opposites fails because those opposites are no clearer than knowledge, making the account circular or more obscure.
rows.anchor: أن هذا تعريف العلم بانتفاء أضداده وليست معرفة هذه الأضداد أقوى من معرفة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge includes conception as well as assent, but conception admits no certainty, doubt, strength, or weakness, so this definition excludes it.
rows.anchor: أن العلم قد يكون تصورا وقد يكون تصديقا والتصور لا يتطرق إليه الجزم ولا التردد ولا القوة ولا الضعف

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila define knowledge as belief that produces tranquility of the soul, or simply whatever produces that tranquility; they treat “tranquility” as an intelligible metaphor.
rows.anchor: العلم هو الإعتقاد المقتضى سكون النفس وربما قالوا العلم ما يقتضي سكون النفس

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Rāzī’s associates object that belief is a genus distinct from knowledge, so knowledge cannot be defined as a kind of belief.
rows.anchor: الإعتقاد جنس مخالف للعلم فلا يجوز جعل العلم منه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila can answer that belief and knowledge share a common element, which is what their definition means by belief.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن بين العلم واعتقاد المقلد قدرا مشتركا فنحن نعني بالاعتقاد ذلك القدر

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Rāzī’s associates say the tranquility definition also excludes God’s knowledge, since it cannot be described as producing tranquility of a soul.
rows.anchor: وهذا التعريف يخرج عنه أيضا علم الله تعالى فإنه لا يجوز أن يقال فيه إنه يقتضي سكون النفس

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: The philosophers define knowledge as a form present in the soul that corresponds to the known object.
rows.anchor: العلم صورة حاصلة في النفس مطابقة للمعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling knowledge a “form” is metaphorical and needs clarification: if a mountain itself exists in the mind, that is impossible; if only its image exists, the image rather than the mountain is known.
rows.anchor: إذا عقلنا الجبل والبحر فإن حصلا في الذهن ففي الذهن جبل وبحر وهذا محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that a mental form corresponds to the known is circular.
rows.anchor: قوله مطابقة للمعلوم يقتضي الدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correspondence cannot explain their abstract objects, such as second intelligibles and mental considerations, which may have no external existence.
rows.anchor: المعلومات قد تكون موجودة في الخارج وقد لا تكون وهي التي يسمونها بالأمور الاعتبارية والصور الذهنية والمعقولات الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People know non-existent things, but correspondence requires two positive entities and therefore cannot relate an image to sheer non-being.
rows.anchor: أنا قد نعقل المعدوم ولا يمكن أن يقال الصورة العقلية مطابقة للمعدوم

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the philosophers’ account by comparing inner perception with sight: an image of the object enters the faculty, while its essence, not its physical body, is meant.
rows.anchor: حاول الغزالي إيضاح كلام الفلاسفة في تعريف العلم فقال إدراك البصيرة الباطنة نفهمه بالمقايسة بالبصر الظاهر

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: In al-Ghazālī’s analogy, the human substance is like iron, intellect like a polished mirror, and the known object like the reflected image.
rows.anchor: جوهر الآدمي كالحديد وعقله كالصقالة والمعلوم كالصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects defining sight as an image impressed in the visual faculty because the definition invokes both the one who sees and the object seen.
rows.anchor: أنه ذكر في تعريف الأبصار المبصر والباصر وهو دور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If sight were the imprint itself, a tiny faculty could not contain an image as large as what is seen; even if a small image is only a condition, that condition differs from seeing.
rows.anchor: لما أبصرنا إلا بمقدار نقطة الناظر لاستحالة انطباع العظيم في الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We see an object where it is; if we saw only its impressed image, we would see it at the image’s location instead.
rows.anchor: أنا نرى المرئي حيث هو ، ولو كان المرئي هو الصورة المنطبعة لما رأيته في حيزه ومكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the mental image of heat has heat’s essence, the intellect becomes hot when thinking of heat; if it does not, the mind has not grasped heat’s essence.
rows.anchor: إما أن تكون مساوية للحرارة في الماهية أو لا تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says leading philosophers agree that an object’s image is not imprinted in a mirror, so al-Ghazālī’s explanation fits neither their position nor their principles.
rows.anchor: اتفق المحققون من الفلاسفة على أن صورة المرئي لا تنطبع في المرآة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to define knowledge can result either from the subject being too obscure or from its being so evident that nothing clearer can define it.
rows.anchor: العجز عن التعريف قد يكون لخفاء المطلوب جدا وقد يكون لبلوغه في الجلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge’s essence is self-evident: everyone necessarily knows that they exist and that they are neither in the sky nor in the depths of the sea.
rows.anchor: كل أحد يعلم بالضرورة أنه يعلم وجود نفسه وأنه يعلم أنه ليس على السماء ولا في لجة البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing a relation entails knowing both its terms; necessary knowledge of such relations therefore makes knowledge’s essence immediately known and impossible to define.
rows.anchor: فلما كان العلم الضروري بهذه المنسوبية حاصلا كان العلم الضروري بماهية العلم حاصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī begins a discussion of thirty words thought to be synonyms for knowledge.
rows.anchor: في البحث عن ألفاظ يظن بها أنها مرادفة للعلم وهي ثلاثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idrāk literally means meeting or reaching; when the intellect reaches and grasps an intelligible essence, this is perception.
rows.anchor: القوة العاقلة إذا وصلت إلى ماهية المعقول وحصلتها كان ذلك إدراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿūr is perception without firm establishment, the first wavering arrival of knowledge in the intellect; God may be described as both perceiving and knowing.
rows.anchor: الشعور وهو إدراك بغير استثبات وهو أول مراتب وصول المعلوم إلى القوة العاقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣawwur is the intellect’s complete grasp of a meaning; the term derives from bodily “form,” by analogy with the mistaken idea that essences inhere in intellect as shapes in matter.
rows.anchor: التصور لفظ مشتق من الصورة ولفظ الصورة حيث وضع فإنما وضع للهيئة الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥifẓ is an acquired mental image made firm enough to recover if lost; God’s knowledge is not called preservation because it cannot weaken or be lost.
rows.anchor: إذا حصلت الصورة في العقل وتأكدت واستحكمت وصارت بحيث لو زالت لتمكنت القوة العاقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhakkur is the mind’s attempt to retrieve a stored image after it has vanished; this seems paradoxical because a present image needs no recovery, while an unnoticed one cannot be sought.
rows.anchor: إذا حاول الذهن استرجاعها فتلك المحاولة هي التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr is the return of an image after its disappearance; an unnamed poet’s line makes prior forgetting a condition, and speech is called remembrance because it brings meaning to mind.
rows.anchor: فالله يعلم أني لست أذكره … وكيف أذكره إذ لست أنساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “remember Me” raises a dilemma: if addressed during forgetfulness the servant is unaware of it, but if after forgetfulness remembrance already exists and cannot be newly produced.
rows.anchor: فهذا الأمر هل يتوجه على العبد حال حصول النسيان أو بعد زواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogous command to know that none is a deity but God concerns assent to monotheism, not conception, so the paradox does not apply as strongly as it does to remembrance.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن المأمور به إنما هو معرفة للتوحيد وهذا من باب التصديقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that introspection confirms people can remember; knowing that capacity suffices for disciplined effort even though the process itself remains unknown.
rows.anchor: نجد من أنفسنا أنه يمكننا التذكر وإذا كان ذلك ممكنا كان ما ذكرته تشكيكا في الضروريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing to grasp how one remembers reveals human limitation; God makes the most evident things mysterious so servants recognize their incapacity and glimpse divine secrets.
rows.anchor: سبحان من جعل أظهر الأشياء أخفاها ليتوصل العبد به إلى كنه عجزه ونهاية قصوره

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: One group distinguishes maʿrifa as knowledge of particulars from ʿilm as knowledge of universals.
rows.anchor: المعرفة إدراك الجزئيات والعلم إدراك الكليات

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group calls maʿrifa conception and ʿilm assent, making maʿrifa higher because human assent to a Necessary Being is certain while grasping God’s essence exceeds human capacity.
rows.anchor: المعرفة التصور والعلم هو التصديق وهؤلاء جعلوا العرفان أعظم درجة من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account every gnostic is learned, but not every learned person is a gnostic; no human truly knows God because grasping His essence is impossible.
rows.anchor: فإن أحدا من البشر لا يعرف الله تعالى لأن الاطلاع على كنه هويته وسر ألوهيته محال

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A further account defines maʿrifa as recognizing a second apprehension of something as the same thing previously perceived.
rows.anchor: ثم أدرك ذلك الشيء ثانيا وعرف أن هذا المدرك الذي أدركه ثانيا هو الذي أدركه أولا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Some who hold souls pre-existed bodies say souls were drawn from Adam, confessed God’s lordship, then forgot Him through bodily darkness and recognize Him again upon release.
rows.anchor: إنها هي الذر المستخرج من صلب آدم عليه السلام وإنها أقرت بالإلهية واعترفت بالربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahm is conceiving something from an interlocutor’s words; ifhām is the conveyance of meaning through wording to the listener’s understanding.
rows.anchor: الفهم وهو تصور الشيء من لفظ المخاطب والإفهام هو اتصال المعنى باللفظ إلى فهم السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiqh is knowing a speaker’s purpose; Qur’an 18:93 describes Quraysh as barely understanding because their doubts and desires kept them from seeing the true benefits and aims of divine duties.
rows.anchor: فقهت كلامك أي وقفت على غرضك من هذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAql is knowledge of qualities such as good, evil, perfection, and deficiency: perceived benefits prompt action, harms prompt restraint, like a camel’s tether.
rows.anchor: العقل وهو العلم بصفات الأشياء من حسنها وقبحها وكمالها ونقصانها

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: When asked what intellect is, one righteous person answered that it is knowing which of two goods is better and which of two evils is worse; the rational person obeys God’s commands.
rows.anchor: هو العلم بخير الخيرين وشر الشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirāya is knowledge reached through a kind of contrivance: arranging premises and using deliberation; its derivation evokes training with a hunting spear and a tool for grooming hair.
rows.anchor: المعرفة الحاصلة بضرب من الحيل وهو تقديم المقدمات واستعمال الروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirāya cannot be attributed to God because thought and contrivance are impossible for Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يصح إطلاقه على الله تعالى لامتناع الفكر والحيل عليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥikma can mean sound knowledge or righteous action, but is more specific to practical than theoretical knowledge and more commonly used for action; God’s wisdom creates benefits and welfare.
rows.anchor: وهي اسم لكل علم حسن ، وعمل صالح وهو بالعلم العملي أخص منه بالعلم النظري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition of wisdom is knowing things as they truly are; it implies knowledge of essences is superior because particulars change while essences endure.
rows.anchor: هي معرفة الأشياء بحقائقها ، وهذا إشارة إلى أن إدراك الجزئيات لا كمال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition calls wisdom performing an act whose outcome is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: هي الإتيان بالفعل الذي عاقبته محمودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further definition is imitating the Creator in governance as far as humanly possible: removing ignorance, injustice, stinginess, and foolishness from one’s knowledge, action, generosity, and forbearance.
rows.anchor: هي الاقتداء بالخالق سبحانه وتعالى في السياسة بقدر الطاقة البشرية

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Certainty requires believing something is so and that its opposite is impossible, based on either intuitive necessity or rational proof.
rows.anchor: إن اليقين لا يحصل إلا إذا اعتقد أن الشيء كذا وأنه يمتنع كون الأمر بخلاف معتقده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mind is the soul’s capacity to acquire knowledge not yet possessed; God creates the spirit ignorant, but for worship, which requires knowledge.
rows.anchor: استعداد النفس لتحصيل هذه المعارف هو الذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides the senses and thought to acquire knowledge: the text links hearing, sight, and reflection to Qur’anic signs and says their cooperation makes the ignorant spirit learned.
rows.anchor: فإذا تطابقت هذه القوى صار الروح الجاهل عالما

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Thought is the soul’s movement from present assents toward assents not yet brought to mind; one investigator likens it to supplication for knowledge from God.
rows.anchor: إن الفكر يجري مجرى التضرع إلى الله تعالى في استنزال العلوم من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intuition is the soul’s readiness to find the middle term linking the two sides of an unknown; that term supplies two premises, like legal witnesses, from which the conclusion follows.
rows.anchor: فاستعداد النفس لوجدان ذلك المتوسط هو الحدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhakāʾ is exceptionally strong, perfected intuition reaching its highest degree: quick, penetrating arrival at truth; its etymology evokes fire, wind, and sharp slaughter.
rows.anchor: الذكاء وهو شدة الحدس وكماله وبلوغه الغاية القصوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiṭna is noticing something deliberately hinted at and is most often used for solving riddles and symbols.
rows.anchor: الفطنة وهي عبارة عن التنبه لشيء قصد تعريضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A khāṭir is the soul’s movement toward obtaining proof; strictly it is the content present in the mind, while the mind is called the thought by naming a container for what it holds.
rows.anchor: الخاطر وهو حركة النفس نحو تحصيل الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahm is a weaker belief, or judgment about particular non-sensible matters involving particular embodied beings, such as a lamb’s bond with its mother.
rows.anchor: الوهم وهو الإعتقاد المرجوح وقد يقال إنه عبارة عن الحكم بأمور جزئية غير محسوسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann is a preponderant belief that still allows its alternative; because belief’s strength is hard to measure, degrees of conjecture are likewise indistinct.
rows.anchor: ترجيح أحد طرفي المعتقد في القلب على الآخر مع تجويز الطرف الآخر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators read “they think they will meet their Lord” as knowledge: worldly knowledge compared with the afterlife is conjecture, or true worldly knowledge is nearly confined to prophets and the truthful.
rows.anchor: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقوا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjecture based on strong evidence is accepted and praiseworthy and underlies most practical judgments; weakly grounded conjecture is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وعليه مدار أكثر أحوال هذا العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayāl is the image that remains from a sensed object after it is absent; it can appear in sleep or waking, while ṭayf is only used for sleep.
rows.anchor: الصورة الباقية عن المحسوس بعد غيبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badīha is knowledge arising immediately in the soul without thought, such as knowing that one is half of two.
rows.anchor: المعرفة الحاصلة ابتداء في النفس لا بسبب الفكر كعلمك بأن الواحد نصف الاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awwaliyyāt are the same as self-evident first principles: the intellect initially joins predicate to subject without an intermediary; with mediation, the middle term is primary.
rows.anchor: الذهن يلحق محمول القضية بموضوعها أولا لا بتوسط شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawiyya is knowledge reached after extensive thought.
rows.anchor: ما كان من المعرفة بعد فكر كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kiyāsa is the soul’s ability to infer what benefits it; the Prophet calls the discerning person one who reckons with himself and works for the afterlife, the greatest good.
rows.anchor: الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khibra is knowledge acquired through experience; Abū al-Dardāʾ says he found people “akhbar taqillahu,” and another derivation compares it to a milk-rich she-camel.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء : وجدت الناس أخبر تقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾy is the mind’s encompassing of premises expected to yield a conclusion, or the conclusion itself; opinion is to thought as a tool is to a maker.
rows.anchor: الرأي ، وهو إحاطة الخاطر في المقدمات التي يرجى منها إنتاج المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two proverbs warn against immature opinion and recommend setting opinion aside to reach the right result.
rows.anchor: إياك والرأي الفطير ، وقيل : دع الرأي تصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firāsa infers inward character from outward signs; Qur’anic references validate the method, and its etymology suggests knowledge seized like a predator taking prey.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال بالحق الظاهر على الخلق الباطن ، وقد نبه الله تعالى على صدق هذا الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of physiognomy arrives spontaneously without a known cause, as inspiration or revelation; the Prophet says there are inspired people in his community, including ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: إن في أمتي لمحدثين وإن عمر لمنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind is a learned craft that infers inward traits from visible forms; exegetes apply the two types to the “witness” in Qur’an 11:17.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال بالأشكال الظاهرة على الأخلاق الباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving divine unity, prophethood, and resurrection and recalling universal favors, God recalls special favors to Israel’s ancestors to break Jewish obstinacy, win their hearts, and signal Muhammad’s prophethood through unseen knowledge.
rows.anchor: كسرا لعنادهم ولجاجهم بتذكير النعم السالفة واستمالة لقلوبهم بسببها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first recalls Israel’s favors generally, then derives a command to believe in Muhammad and discusses what blocks belief.
rows.anchor: وفرع على تذكيرها الأمر بالإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeats the general reminder because the Israelites are deeply heedless, then pairs the promise of preference above the worlds with a severe warning about the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على شدة غفلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī regards this progression from general reminder to inducement and warning, then detailed blessings, as ideal ordering for invitation and establishing belief in the listener.
rows.anchor: هذا هو النهاية في حسن الترتيب لمن يريد الدعوة وتحصيل الإعتقاد في قلب المستمع

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators agree that Israel is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham.
rows.anchor: اتفق المفسرون على أن إسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They explain Israel as “servant of God,” deriving Isra as servant and El as God, as in the names Gabriel and Michael.
rows.anchor: إن معنى إسرائيل عبد الله لأن ( إسرا ) في لغتهم هو العبد و ( إيل ) هو الله

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl offers a different etymology: in Hebrew Isra means “human,” so Israel means “man of God.”
rows.anchor: قال القفال : قيل إن ( إسرا ) بالعبرانية في معنى إنسان فكأنه قيل رجل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Jews in Medina during Muhammad’s time, descendants of Jacob.
rows.anchor: خطاب مع جماعة اليهود الذين كانوا بالمدينة من ولد يعقوب عليه السلام في أيام محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
